name: nominatim-bdd-au
description: Hand-translated from osm-search/Nominatim BDD feature files under test/bdd/features/api/{search,reverse}/. Nominatim's own scenarios use a Liechtenstein test database; each case below preserves the scenario shape (what behaviour is being asserted) but swaps the inputs for AU data we actually have. Notes on each case point back to the source scenario.

cases.notes: Source: test/bdd/features/api/search/structured.feature — 'Structured search for street with housenumber, city and postcode'. Validates that a fully-structured query returns the house_number + road.

Source: 'Structured search for country only'. We don't have a dedicated country-only structured path, but a search using the country_code alone + an empty q should not 500 — it returns nothing or a country centroid, both are fine.

Source: 'Structured search for street with housenumber, city and bad postcode'. In Nominatim, a wrong postcode doesn't prevent the hit because the street-and-city signal is strong enough. Our schema doesn't take postcode as a query param, so we model the same tolerance by submitting the correct structured fields and noting the postcode-equivalence expectation via the response's address.postcode.
Source: 'House number search for non-street address' (`6 Silum, Liechtenstein`). AU equivalent: '10 Alysse Close Baulkham Hills'. Asserts the freeform query still resolves to the G-NAF house number.
Source: 'With missing housenumber search falls back to road'. An implausibly-large housenumber should fall back to the street centroid, returning no house_number but still naming the road.

Source: 'Reverse - Address with numerical house number' (coord near Schmedgässle 6). AU equivalent: the G-NAF house-point at 10 Alysse Close. Validates that reverse returns road-level detail (house_number emission depends on whether the coord is close enough to a G-NAF point).

Source: 'Reverse - Unknown countries fall back to default country grid'. Their behaviour returns 'United States' for an unmapped coord in North America. Our equivalent: a coord outside AU (our only index) should not crash — the response may have sparse fields but status 200 is the contract.

Source: 'Reverse - Zoom levels below 5 result in country'. We don't expose a zoom parameter, but the equivalent signal is 'coord inside AU returns AU country_code'. Pins the country detection at a rural coord.

Source: 'Search for natural object' (`Samina` → waterway in Austria). AU equivalent: 'Yarra' — the Yarra River is prominent and its name also matches suburbs; a search should return something sensible. Permissive check (results array exists + first hit's country is AU) because our ranking between place vs stream vs suburb is implementation-defined.
